name: Intersafe - Scam & Malware Protection
description: Real-time browser protection that stops scams, malicious scripts, fake verification pages, and social engineering attacks.
_comment_optional_permissions: management and privacy are requested ON DEMAND, the first time someone opens Security Checkup, not at install. They produce Chrome's two most alarming install-prompt lines ('manage your apps, extensions and themes' and 'change your privacy settings') and are used by NOTHING except the checkup -- core ClickFix/clipboard protection does not touch either. Asking at install charges the scariest permission cost before the user has seen any value, which is a known driver of install abandonment. Verified before moving these: every chrome.management and chrome.privacy call site in background.ts is inside runSecurityCheckup, applyCheckupFix, applyCheckupRevert, or the removeExtension handler. If a future feature needs either API outside the checkup, it must request them the same way -- do NOT move these back to required.
_comment_match_origin_as_fallback: Closes a real bypass: "<all_urls>" does not match the about:, data:, blob: or filesystem: schemes, so with all_frames alone NO content script ran inside an <iframe srcdoc="...">, and injected.js was absent too since the content script is what injects it. Copy events do not cross document boundaries, so the parent frame's copy block never saw a copy made inside the child -- an attacker could host the whole 'press Win+R and paste' lure in a srcdoc frame and neither clipboard layer would fire. Verified with test/fake-captcha-srcdoc.html before and after. This is a BOOLEAN; an audit suggested the string "match_for_about_scheme", which is not a valid Chrome value and would be silently ignored, so it was checked against Chrome's content_scripts docs first. NOT a permission change, so the Web Store per-permission justifications are unaffected. It does mean the content script now runs in more frames, so keep it in mind for the release perf pass.
